entries.one_line: GCN defines the localized spectral propagation rule that almost every molecular encoder inherits; the receptive field is one hop per layer.
MPNN unifies message-passing models for molecules and fixes a neighbourhood radius per step.
Systematic study of graph pretraining objectives; naive pretraining can hurt, and the unlabelled corpus is used as one fixed pool.
MolCLR builds contrastive positives by atom masking, bond deletion and subgraph removal over the full unlabelled pool.
InfoGraph maximises mutual information between graph- and substructure-level representations, agnostic to which unlabelled graphs are used.
GROVER pretrains a graph transformer on eleven million unlabelled molecules with node/edge self-supervision.
k-centre core-set selection for images; the guarantee is stated for a fixed feature space.
SchNet's continuous-filter convolution gives rotation/translation invariant molecular representations, trained from scratch per task.
Selects pretraining molecules by expected informativeness for the label budget; ignores the cost of the corpus itself.
Power-law scaling of downstream error against corpus size on a fixed, uncurated corpus.
